correctness.rationale: A normal in v_i^⊥ avoiding the other generator orthogonality hyperplanes exposes exactly a translate of [0,v_i]; every such edge is obtained from its relative-interior normal cone. Distinct sign chambers cannot expose the same edge: using the opposite endpoint of even one nonorthogonal generator strictly loses its support contribution. For fixed n, outside finitely many vertex offsets the vertices of the section are exactly transverse intersections with edges (a point in the relative interior of a higher-dimensional face cannot be an isolated extreme point of the section). Each edge contributes its projected interval length; edges perpendicular to n contribute zero, so no genericity in n is needed. Dividing the finite sum by the Minkowski-sum support width proves the formula. If the ratio is constant c, crossing only the i-th generator orthogonality hyperplane forces a slope jump of 2(r_i−c)||v_i||² to vanish. Independent generator d-subsets make the restrictions to v_i^⊥ a general-position central arrangement, with m−1 hyperplanes in dimension d−1 and therefore the stated region count. In d=3 the number of distinct restricted lines equals the number of distinct generator pair planes and each line contributes two sectors. Independently normalized the pairwise cross products in the three examples, obtaining zone counts (6,6,6,6), (8,8,8,8,8,8), and (4,4,4,6). In the balanced example the two other generators in the same plane together contribute one common span; three more generators give three separate mixed spans. This clarifies the wording in the example without changing any result.

evidence: Theorem 2.1 allows centrally symmetric polytopes, not just zonotopes, and identifies zonotopes with equal edge multiplicities as exactly the constant-mean subclass.

Theorem 1.1 and §6 express the three-dimensional multiplicities as twice the number of maximal generator spans containing each generator. Shephard and Holtz–Ron give the classical zone and normal-fan framework.

evidence: Bárány–Domokos use the same average over the full support interval with direction fixed, not a central section or a motion-invariant line/hyperplane measure.

Their general edge-projection numerator in (3.1) counts each edge for all offsets between its endpoints. For a pairwise nonparallel generator representation this becomes the sum of r_i times the projected length of v_i; the support width is the corresponding sum without r_i.

originality.rationale: Bárány and Domokos, Same average in every direction, arXiv:2310.18960v2, explicitly prove the equal-edge-multiplicity iff for the same fixed-normal uniform-offset expectation (Theorem 2.1), under the more general hypothesis of central symmetry. Their equation (3.1) is the edge-projection formula and Theorem 1.1 with §6 gives the precise three-dimensional degree characterization. Their Example 6.2 already includes the balanced six-generator arrangement presented here. The generic arrangement count is a classical direct corollary and does not leave a distinct result of the frozen scope. This is demonstrated prior coverage, not a failed search or uncertain attribution.
residual_risks: The inspected Swan passage did not establish whether he explicitly notes the parallelotope extension elsewhere; the implication by affine equivalence is clear.
The exact chronology of distinct same-day catalogue records is not established and is irrelevant to the older primary theorem.
